selfReported: Framework gap: my first test used Sygnal's `renderComponent` and failed before reaching my code.
Its mock DOM doesn't support `.data()`, which the app's existing `TOGGLE` intent uses (`DOM.change('.toggle').data('id', Number)`); the error was `DOM.change(...).data is not a function`.
Any app that uses the `.data()`, `.value()` or similar helpers would hit this, so `renderComponent` should probably be fixed in the sygnal repo.

selfReported: Problems in Sygnal that will affect other people:
The Vite plugin breaks test files that call `run(App)`. It rewrites the line to `app = const __sygnal = run(App)`, which is a syntax error.
`renderComponent` mocks are missing the DOM shorthands. The mocked DOM source has no `DOM.input()` or `.value()`, so the existing Editor code fails with "DOM.input(...).value is not a function".

selfReported: Sygnal Vite plugin bug: the plugin rewrites any test file that calls `run(App)` and injects HMR code that points to a variable outside its scope.
My workaround is a comment in the test file that mentions `import.meta.hot`, which makes the plugin skip that file.
It should be fixed in `src/vite/plugin.ts` in the library: either skip the rewrite when `run()` is called inside a function, or turn it off when tests run under Vitest.

selfReported: Two Sygnal problems came up that are worth fixing in the framework:
Fetch failures are swallowed by `driverFromAsync`. When its function rejects, it only logs the error and sends nothing back to the app, so an error message would never appear.
The Sygnal Vite plugin breaks test files that call `run(App, ...)`. It treats such a file as the app entry and rewrites it for hot reload, even under vitest.
